title: Forgot PIN: let the warden export a backup without unlocking, then reset
description: Product Owner question: what happens if the warden forgets their PIN. Today they lose everything - a grep for 'forgot', 'reset' or 'recover' across the app returns nothing, and being deliberately accountless and offline there is no email or server fallback either. The only way back in is clearing app data or reinstalling, which destroys every hostel, tenant, invoice and payment. DECIDED - option (a), export-then-reset. The lock screen gains a 'Forgot PIN?' route that does two things in order: first it runs the existing LODGY-28 backup export straight to SAF, without ever entering the app; then, once the warden has a file in hand, it offers to reset the PIN by clearing the stored hash. After setting a new PIN they import the backup and are whole again. The rejected alternatives and why: a recovery code (wardens who will not retype a paper register will not store a code, and it is only as safe as wherever they put it); a security question (answers are guessable by exactly the people physically near the phone, which is the threat model); revealing or silently resetting the PIN with no export (makes the lock decorative). WHY THIS IS CHEAP AND SAFE: the PIN gates the UI, not the data. AppRootViewModel merely picks between Locked and Unlocked, and the database is not encrypted (DESIGN.md 5, an accepted MVP decision). So the records already survive a forgotten PIN intact - this ticket only adds a sanctioned way to reach them, and reuses an export path that exists and is tested. THE HONEST TRADE-OFF, accepted deliberately: this does let anyone holding the phone take a backup of the tenant data without knowing the PIN. That is a real widening, and it is accepted because the threat model is one warden's own phone guarding rent records from casual snooping, not a determined attacker - and because the data is already extractable from an unencrypted database by anyone with the phone and a cable. The realistic disaster here is a locked-out warden, not a thief. The reset half must still be treated as destructive and confirmed as such. SEQUENCING NOTE: LODGY-46 finding 3 (no backoff or lockout on repeated PIN attempts) is still open and has no ticket of its own. It was correctly held back because a lockout without recovery would only make this failure arrive faster - with this ticket built, that objection goes away and a lockout becomes safe to add.
acceptanceCriteria: The lock screen offers a discoverable 'Forgot PIN?' route, visible at the moment it is needed rather than hidden in settings
That route exports a full backup via SAF without unlocking the app, reusing LODGY-28's export rather than a second copy of it
The PIN reset is offered only after the export, and the flow states plainly that the app's data will be cleared and that the backup is how it comes back
The reset is confirmed explicitly before anything is destroyed, following the LODGY-57 confirmation pattern
If the warden declines or cancels the export, no reset happens and nothing is lost
If biometric unlock is enrolled, the warden is pointed at it first, before any destructive step
After setting a new PIN, importing that backup restores the data intact - verified as a full round trip, not assumed
Backward compatible: an existing install is unaffected until the warden uses the route, and no migration is required
USER-MANUAL.md documents the route, since the warden will be reading it in a panic

history.note: Filed after the PO asked what happens on a forgotten PIN. Verified in code: no recovery path exists at all, and being accountless and offline there is no email or server fallback either, so the only way back in is clearing data and losing everything. Mitigating factor also verified - the PIN gates the UI, not the data, and the database is not encrypted, so the records survive and only access to them is lost. Filed High because the failure is total and permanent for anyone without a recent backup.

DECIDED: option (a) - export a backup from the lock screen without unlocking, then offer to reset the PIN. Recovery code, security question and bare reset all rejected, reasons recorded in the description. Acceptance criteria rewritten from the option-comparison set to the buildable one. The trade-off is accepted with eyes open: this lets anyone holding the phone take a backup without the PIN, which is a real widening but a small one given the database is already unencrypted and extractable with a cable. Also noted that this unblocks LODGY-46 finding 3 - attempt lockout was held back because a lockout without recovery makes the lockout permanent, and that objection is now answered.

Cross-reference: LODGY-77 now tracks the PIN attempt-delay from security review finding 3, and depends on this ticket shipping first. Note its AC that the forgot-PIN route added here must stay reachable while a delay is in effect - a warden who has genuinely forgotten must not have to wait out a penalty to reach their way out.

Starting the PO's decided option (a): a 'Forgot PIN?' route on the lock screen that first exports a full backup via SAF without unlocking (reusing LODGY-28's BackupManager.export, not a second copy), then - only after a file is in hand - offers to reset the PIN by clearing the stored warden hash, confirmed as destructive per LODGY-57. If biometric is enrolled, point the warden at it first. No schema change, no migration (AC8).

Surfacing a real interaction for the PO rather than deciding it silently. Because the PIN gates the UI and not the data, a forgotten-PIN RESET leaves all data in place - so the 'then import the backup' step in the decided flow is a safety net, not a requirement; after resetting and setting a new PIN the warden is already whole. The wrinkle: the backup is exported at forgot-time, so it captures the OLD (forgotten) PIN hash, and PIN LENGTH lives in DataStore which is outside the backup. If the warden later actually RESTORES that specific zip, it re-imposes the old PIN (and a possibly mismatched length) - recoverable by using Forgot PIN again, so not a dead end, but worth a deliberate product call. This is really a property of the existing LODGY-28/29 backup/restore (auth rides inside the DB snapshot), not new to this ticket. Options if you want it smoother: keep the current device's warden row across a restore, or include pinLength in the backup. Left as-is pending your call; the core recovery works and is safe.

Built the PO's decided option (a) and verified the full round trip on the emulator.

WHAT WAS BUILT.
- PinLockScreen gains a 'Forgot PIN?' link below the keypad (AC1). Tapping it opens a recovery screen (state in PinLockViewModel): if biometric is enrolled it points there first (AC6); a 'Save a backup' button runs the LODGY-28 export straight to SAF without unlocking (AC2, reuses BackupManager.export - no second copy); and the 'Reset PIN' button appears ONLY after an export has succeeded (AC3). Reset is behind a LODGY-57-style confirm dialog (AC4). Cancelling the export leaves everything as-is (AC5).
- Reset BLANKS the warden's pinHash rather than deleting the row. First cut deleted it and crashed with SQLiteConstraintException FOREIGN KEY - hostels FK to warden.id. Fix: WardenRepository.clearWarden() updates the row to an empty hash; AppRootViewModel treats null-or-empty hash as NeedsPinSetup; PinSetup now calls WardenRepository.setPin() which UPDATES the existing row (or inserts on true first launch), so the id and every hostel FK survive. No schema change, no migration (AC8).

VERIFIED ON DEVICE (Hindi UI), full round trip:
- Lock screen showed 'Forgot PIN?'. Opened it - no Reset button yet. Saved a backup via the SAF picker; a valid zip was written (pulled it: lodgy.db with all 3 hostels / 6 tenants / 6 agreements / 7 invoices / 7 payments). THEN the Reset button appeared.
- Reset -> confirm -> confirmed. No crash; app went to the PIN-setup screen. Set a new 4-digit PIN 1111, confirmed, and the app unlocked straight to the dashboard with every property and figure intact (AC7).
- DB check: warden row is the SAME id as before (19541e52), hash re-set, and zero hostels orphaned - the FK held throughout. Data counts identical to pre-reset.

NOTE the emulator PIN is now 1111 (4-digit), changed by this test.

OPEN FOR THE PO (see the comment above, not a defect): restoring the forgot-time backup would re-impose the old forgotten PIN. Pre-existing to LODGY-28/29.

489 tests pass (was 481; +8), line coverage 97.00% (gate 0.93), jacocoCoverageVerification green, assembleDebug OK.

Docs updated in step: DESIGN.md 4.1 (with the known-interaction note) + two decision-log rows; USER-MANUAL.md 1; two figures in docs/design/screenshots.html. No DATA-MODEL.md change - no schema change.

PASS - verified the full round trip on the emulator, and every acceptance criterion holds with one wording divergence flagged for the PO below.

AC1 'Forgot PIN?' is right on the lock screen. AC2 it exports a full backup via SAF without unlocking, reusing the LODGY-28 export - pulled the written zip and confirmed it holds lodgy.db with all 3 hostels / 6 tenants / 6 agreements / 7 invoices / 7 payments. AC3 the Reset button appears only AFTER a successful export - not before. AC4 reset is behind an explicit LODGY-57 confirm dialog. AC5 backing out before exporting leaves everything intact and clears nothing. AC6 the biometric-first hint and button are shown when a fingerprint is enrolled (code-verified; the emulator has none enrolled). AC7 THE ROUND TRIP: reset -> new 4-digit PIN -> app unlocked straight to a dashboard with every property and figure intact; the warden row kept its original id, its hash was re-set, and zero hostels were orphaned, so the hostels->warden foreign key held throughout. AC8 no schema change, no migration. AC9 USER-MANUAL section 1 documents the route.

Also confirmed the crash the developer hit and fixed is gone: deleting the warden row failed a FOREIGN KEY constraint; blanking the hash and reusing the row on setup is correct and does not crash.

DIVERGENCE FLAGGED FOR THE PO, not failing the ticket: AC3 as written says the flow should state 'the app's data will be CLEARED and that the backup is how it comes back'. The built flow states the opposite - 'Your data stays. Only the PIN is cleared' - because the implemented reset is deliberately non-destructive (it blanks the hash; the data survives, as the ticket's own premise notes). Telling the warden their data will be cleared would be false, so the messaging is correct for the actual behaviour. The developer already raised this as a comment for the PO (restoring a forgot-time backup re-imposes the old PIN). Passing on the basis that the behaviour is safe and correct; the PO should ratify the reworded AC3 at acceptance.

Accepted, and it is better than I expected. The forgot-PIN screen makes me save a backup before it will reset anything, and it says outright that my hostels, tenants and payments stay on the phone and only the PIN is cleared. That last line is exactly what I would need to read while panicking. With no account and no internet there is no other way back in, so making the backup mandatory first is the right call.
